segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.

And they entered the country of Cilicia,
and remained in it fifteen days, taking captives and plundering.
For ten days they camped against Anazarba,
and brought great distress upon the inhabitants of the country
who had fled thither.
And if they had delayed over it a little more,
they would have taken it because of the lack of water;
but God drove them away.
They completely burned the monastery of Paximates,
and likewise the monastery of Rabban Qawma.
To Guklak, however, they did not reach.
And as soon as they reached Syria,
this breach {disaffection} became evident to the ruler of Egypt,
who was the son of Bunduqdar.
And he departed in haste from Damascus,
and went to Egypt.
And when he began to assemble forces,
those who were with Baysari dispersed,
because they were afraid of the Sultan.
He, however, when he was left alone, went to Jerusalem,
and clung to the Porch of Solomon,
and shaved the hair of his head,
offering repentance for his folly.
Now that elder son of Bunduqdar,
when he saw that division had fallen among his forces,
went up to the fortress of Karak,
and released himself from the kingdom.
And the grandees assembled,
and swore allegiance to his younger brother,
and seated him on the royal throne in Egypt;
but he did not succeed.
Rather, a certain emir named Alfi rose up against him,
and drove him out,
and he himself reigned in Egypt.
And in this summer, the son of Sultan Izz al-Din, the ruler of the country of the Romans, fled from the territory of Barkah,
and came to Abaqa,
and he received him joyfully.
And when he desired to give him half of the country of the Romans,
the grandees did not permit it.
For they said,
"If this happens,
dispute will increase between him and the son of his uncle."
And they undertook to give him half the revenue of the whole country,
while authority over any place he should not have.
And he agreed to this,
even though not of his own will.
And in the year 1591,
(1591 of the Greeks?), Ashmut, the Uighur emir, and Mas'ud Bar Qawti approached King of Kings Abaqa,
and showed that the judges who had been sent with Baba the Persian had wronged them,
and that fifteen {OCR?} had been served by bribery.
Seventeen {OCR?}.
